sections.heading: C — Your Driver's License
sections.markdown:
## C — Your Driver's License

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Any person who drives a car, motorcycle, or moped on public roads in Iowa must hold a permit or license [A01].
Why it matters: this is the chapter threshold rule, and every exemption after it is an exception to this sentence.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Registering to vote in Iowa counts you as a resident for driver licensing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Enrolling a child in an Iowa public school counts you as a resident for driver licensing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Taking a permanent job in Iowa counts you as a resident for driver licensing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
Living in Iowa without a break for 30 days counts you as a resident for driver licensing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
Claiming a homestead or military tax exemption on Iowa property counts you as a resident for driver licensing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Getting public assistance from the state counts you as a resident for driver licensing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Meeting any single one of the residency triggers is enough to count as an Iowa resident for licensing [A01].
Why it matters: candidates often think several triggers must combine, but the handbook requires only one.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
Service members driving military vehicles while on duty do not need an Iowa license [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
Farm machinery may move between the home farm and nearby fields or farm sites within two miles with no license needed [A01].
Why it matters: the exemption is narrow, covering equipment only and only near the home farm.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
Visitors and students may drive in Iowa on a valid license from their home state or country [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
Keep your license or permit with you every time you drive [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Motorists must also keep current registration proof plus a paper or electronic insurance card showing liability coverage [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Missing paperwork can mean fines and possible impoundment of your vehicle [A02].
Why it matters: the penalty attaches to the missing documents, not just to the driving.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
Every applicant must complete a vision screening when applying for a license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Every applicant must pass the knowledge test to qualify for a license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
Drivers younger than 18 must show they finished a state-approved driver education course [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
A behind-the-wheel driving test is required unless you already satisfied the driver education course requirement [A02].
Why it matters: driver education can waive the driving test, never the knowledge test.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
Iowa DOT publishes an online practice test on its website to help you study for the knowledge test [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
Drivers under 18 are covered by the Graduated Driver's License Program, with details on the DOT website [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
Iowa offers a Skip the Trip option for taking the knowledge test at home or school, with details on the DOT website [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
Moped licenses and commercial licenses are separate license types with their own requirements on the DOT website [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
The handbook sends readers to the DOT website for when and how to renew a license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0005]

Misconceptions: newcomers often assume an out-of-state license works indefinitely, but any single residency trigger creates an Iowa licensing duty; farm plates do not bless every farm errand, only equipment moved near the home farm.

Mnemonic: vote, school, job, thirty days, tax break, aid — any one trigger makes you an Iowa resident for licensing.

Glossary: resident (a person meeting any licensing trigger); permit (a credential to carry while driving, like a license); liability insurance (coverage every driver must prove with a card); vision screening (the required eyesight check at application); knowledge test (the rules test every applicant must pass); Graduated Driver's License Program (staged licensing for drivers under eighteen); Skip the Trip (knowledge testing at home or school).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
